example.name: sprint_planning_full_flow
example.scenario: The team wants to plan the next sprint. The user asks the Scrum Master agent to run sprint planning.

step.expected_outcome: Platform state and declared vocabulary loaded
List of candidate stories for the sprint

step.action: Check each candidate against the Definition of Ready checklist
step.analysis: Flag items missing acceptance criteria, estimates, or dependencies. These items should not enter Planning.

step.action: Call `scrum_plan_sprint` with selected stories and sprint goal
step.expected_outcome: Stories assigned to the next sprint
Template ready for drafting the planning document

example.completion: Sprint planning complete. Stories [A, B, C] assigned to the next sprint with goal "Implement authentication flow". Planning document template is ready for review.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Always check DoR before adding stories to a sprint
Confirm the sprint goal with the team
Use the ceremony template for structured documentation

example.name: impediment_resolution
example.scenario: A team member reports a blocker during standup that prevents progress on a story.
example.user_request: Story #15 is blocked — waiting on the design team for asset approvals.

step.action: Call `scrum_log_impediment` with description and affected story
Report the impediment logged and next steps per impediment protocol

example.completion: Impediment logged on story #15: "Waiting on design team for asset approvals." Per impediment protocol: investigate today, escalate if no progress by day 2.

example.name: retrospective_drafting
example.scenario: The team wants to run a retrospective at the end of the sprint.

step.action: Compose retro document with data gathering, insights, and one committed improvement

example.completion: Retrospective document drafted with velocity trend data and ceremony template. One committed improvement captured for the next sprint.
